populationLayout.rationale: The leading Total row preserves pooled-only metrics. The participant flow and Figures 2, 3, 5, and 6 directly report compatible values for each of five seasons; season is the strongest directly reported extraction axis.

caveats: Pooled injury count remains blank because the source reports 224 in Results prose, 229 in severity prose, while the five direct Figure 2 season counts sum to 226.
Pooled overall incidence retains 8.9 from the abstract and Results with CI 8.72-9.0; the Discussion reports 8.49.
Time-loss units alternate between missed training sessions and days. Stored season totals are transparent contact plus non-contact component sums from Figure 3.
Figure 4 pooled knee count 32 replaces the prior position-table aggregation of 35. The combined Foot-Ankle count is not forced into separate foot or ankle count rows.
The paper explicitly identifies a professional men's team and lack of female participants, so sex is corrected to male.

notes.body: Prospective five-season Turkish Super League surveillance extracted as Total / Goalkeeper / Defenders / Midfielders / Forwards. Conflicting source injury totals of 224, 229 and 227 were not reconciled, so total injury count remains blank. The repeated abstract/Results incidence of 8.9 per 1,000 combined hours is retained with its reported 8.72-9.0 CI, while the conflicting Discussion value of 8.49 remains a review caveat. Injury time loss 4,457 is a transparent sum of direct components, although the paper alternates between sessions and days.

screening.title: Exploring injury profiles in professional football: evidence from a five-year study and the role of the functional movement screen.
screening.ai_reason: A prospective five-season cohort of Turkish Super League football players used club medical surveillance and publishes training, match and combined injury rates per 1,000 hours.
screening.ai_evidence_quote: Our study is based on data collected from professional football players from a football team in the Turkish Super League during the 2016–2017, 2017–2018, 2018–2019, 2019–2020, and 2020–2021 seasons. This was a prospective cohort study in which the players’ injury status and functional movement analysis results were tracked to assess injury prediction.

ai_raw_response.title: Exploring injury profiles in professional football: evidence from a five-year study and the role of the functional movement screen.
ai_raw_response.reason: A prospective five-season cohort of Turkish Super League football players used club medical surveillance and publishes training, match and combined injury rates per 1,000 hours.
ai_raw_response.auditNotes: Although the paper studies FMS prediction as well as injury profile, it prospectively follows an eligible football cohort and reports actual injuries with numeric time-based rates.
ai_raw_response.dataSource: Club sports physicians, specialist doctors and club physiotherapist using a standard injury form.
ai_raw_response.evidenceQuote: Our study is based on data collected from professional football players from a football team in the Turkish Super League during the 2016–2017, 2017–2018, 2018–2019, 2019–2020, and 2020–2021 seasons. This was a prospective cohort study in which the players’ injury status and functional movement analysis results were tracked to assess injury prediction.
evidenceQuotes: Our study is based on data collected from professional football players from a football team in the Turkish Super League during the 2016–2017, 2017–2018, 2018–2019, 2019–2020, and 2020–2021 seasons. This was a prospective cohort study in which the players’ injury status and functional movement analysis results were tracked to assess injury prediction.

Over the five seasons, the injury incidence was 7.76 injuries per 1,000 training hours (95% CI: 7.59–7.93), 15.47 injuries per 1,000 match hours (95% CI: 15.23–15.71), and 8.9 injuries per 1,000 combined hours (95% CI: 8.72- 9.0).

Each injury was recorded immediately after the incident using a standard injury form, which included the type of injury, injury location, duration of absence from training due to the injury, and timing of the injury.
ai_raw_response.competitionContext: Turkish Super League seasons, including match and training activity.
ai_raw_response.outcomeEligibility: Time-loss football injuries and illnesses, with injury profile and incidence outcomes.
ai_raw_response.reportedDenominator: Published training, match and combined injury rates per 1,000 hours.
ai_raw_response.dataCollectionTiming: Player injury status and functional movement analysis were tracked through the 2016–2017 to 2020–2021 seasons.
ai_raw_response.populationEligibility: Professional football players from one Turkish Super League team.
ai_raw_response.injuryIllnessDefinition: Injuries preventing participation in subsequent training, categorised by time loss and recorded immediately after the incident.
ai_raw_response.denominatorEvidenceQuote: Over the five seasons, the injury incidence was 7.76 injuries per 1,000 training hours (95% CI: 7.59–7.93), 15.47 injuries per 1,000 match hours (95% CI: 15.23–15.71), and 8.9 injuries per 1,000 combined hours (95% CI: 8.72- 9.0).
